title: Chicken Tikka Masala
subtitle: The British national dish
excerpt: Marinated chicken, charred under a hot grill, then simmered in a spiced tomato and cream sauce. The great British-Indian curry: creamy, gently spiced, and deeply satisfying.

recipe.sourceNotes: Chicken tikka masala is widely claimed as the unofficial national dish of Britain. Its precise origin is disputed: it is most likely a British-Indian restaurant creation, invented some time in the 1970s, possibly in Glasgow. The dish combines chicken tikka (pieces marinated in spiced yoghurt and grilled in a tandoor or under a grill) with a creamy tomato sauce developed to suit British tastes for milder, creamier curries. Glasgow's Ali Ahmed Aslam of the Shish Mahal restaurant is one of the most often cited inventors.

content.text: The char on the chicken is not optional. Grilling the marinated pieces under a very hot grill until they catch at the edges gives the dish its characteristic smoky note. If you put raw chicken directly into the sauce you get a different result entirely. Make the sauce in advance if you like; it keeps well in the fridge for two days and is better reheated.
Mix the chicken with the yoghurt, garlic, ginger, garam masala, chilli powder, half the turmeric, and a teaspoon of salt. Marinate for at least 2 hours, or overnight in the fridge.
Grill the marinated chicken pieces under a very hot grill for 8 to 10 minutes, turning once, until charred in patches and just cooked through. Set aside.

Heat the oil in a large pan. Cook the onion for 12 minutes until deep golden. Add the garlic, ginger, and cardamom and cook for 2 minutes. Add the coriander, cumin, paprika, and remaining turmeric. Stir for 1 minute. Add the tomato puree and cook for 2 minutes. Add the tinned tomatoes and season. Simmer for 15 minutes.

Add the cream and stir through. Add the grilled chicken and any resting juices. Simmer gently for 5 minutes. Add the garam masala and stir through. Scatter with coriander. Serve with basmati rice and naan.
